correctness.rationale: A primitive square-zero 2-by-2 matrix over each quotient R/(pi^e) is conjugate to the single Jordan nilpotent block, by a primitive image vector and Nakayama reduction; the invertible centralizer gives exactly (q^2-1)q^(2e-2) such matrices. Low entry-valuations k<ceil(n/2) correspond bijectively to primitive lifts of square-zero reductions modulo pi^(n-2k). A unit cofactor proves uniform determinant fibers, and Smith form converts determinant valuations to the asserted image lengths. The complementary high-valuation cone is automatically square-zero and splits by residue rank and determinant valuation. Summation gives the spectrum, total and maximum image length. The standalone checker enumerated all four entries and their entire additive images in twelve finite rings, including mixed characteristic and an extension field; this checks but does not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected commuting-matrix results provide qualitative feasible Jordan partitions, rather than the finite-field frequency of every square-zero Jordan type in a two-equal-block nilpotent centralizer. The full theorem also covers all finite commutative chain rings, gives the entire image-length spectrum, and proves valuation-layer equinumerosity. Existing triangular-matrix square-zero counts and Drazin-index bibliographic results are not the same implication. Searches did not identify an exact published formula; archival partial-access and general Hall-polynomial implications remain acknowledged uncertainties.

value.rationale: The fixed two-equal-block nilpotent centralizer is a canonical module endomorphism algebra; the counts exactly measure the square-zero elements by Jordan type rather than merely stating that those types exist. The theorem also supplies a new length-refined uniform law for all finite commutative chain rings, across equal and mixed characteristic. Exact equinumerosity of the nonautomatic valuation strata and the closed maximal-image formula are structural consequences of the decomposition, useful for nilpotent-commuting-pair statistics and validating local-ring matrix calculations.
